A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work and contain 22 pages, including Appendices A–F. Text extraction and rendered-page comparisons support reliable comparison of the text, figures, tables, equations, and proofs.

before.justification: v2 reports original DirGINE classification, size-generalization, and interpretability experiments, including Figure 4, Table 1, and the edge-removal results in Section 5.2.1.

after.justification: v3 retains these original classification, size-generalization, and interpretability results, including the supplementary examples in Appendix F.

M1.justification: The four-layer, width-32 DirGINE, directed message passing, training objectives, and PGExplainer procedure remain unchanged in Sections 3–4 and Appendix B.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same six quiver families and retain the same training coverage, 11-node test set, and size-generalization evaluation on 12–20 nodes.

E2.justification: No evaluated comparator is added, removed, or revised. The corrected Vatne citations concern existing mathematical results, not new empirical baselines.

E3.justification: The data splits, sample counts in Table 2, generation procedures, evaluation metrics, 50-epoch training budget, and PGExplainer training on 1,000 instances for five epochs are unchanged.

E4.justification: Both retain the size-generalization analysis, edge-removal experiment, latent-space analyses, and Appendix F examples. No ablation, robustness test, or supplementary analysis is added or revised.

E5.justification: Figure 4 retains averaging over 10 training trials, and Section 5.2 retains the same uncertainty reporting for linear classification. No run-count, seed, or statistical-reporting change appears.

E6.justification: Results match throughout: 99.2% test accuracy, Table 1 accuracies including 99.6% at 12 nodes and 89.1% at 20 nodes, and 99.7 ± 0.0% linear-classifier accuracy. Edge-removal findings and supplementary examples also match.

T1.justification: Definitions, mathematical statements, and proofs—including Theorem 6.1 and Appendices D–E—are unchanged. Theorem 5.3 and Lemma D.6 receive corrected author attributions without changes to their mathematics.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims about recovering known type-D structure and independently discovering and proving the affine-D characterization. No contribution or novelty claim changes.

C2.justification: The explanations and qualifications concerning train/test class mismatch, limited GNN depth, post-hoc interpretability, and out-of-distribution edge-removal outputs remain unchanged in Sections 4–6.

D1.justification: Appendices B–C retain the same architecture details, explainer hyperparameters, Sage/PyTorch Geometric processing, sampling instructions, optimizer settings, and GPU specification. No technical or resource-access disclosure changes.

R1.justification: The malformed author name for the 2010 paper The mutation class of Dn quivers is corrected to Vatne; its title, journal, and DOI match. This is a bibliographic correction, with no change to cited-work membership or research positioning.

P1.justification: v3 replaces malformed 'and (2010)' citations with 'Vatne (2010)' throughout the affected main-text and Appendix D passages, corrects the bibliography author, and updates the arXiv stamp. The narrative and section structure otherwise remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Corrected citations cause small local line-wrapping changes, particularly in Sections 2.1 and 5. All figures, tables, diagrams, captions, and their placement remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: v3 repairs recurring malformed citations and the bibliography attribution to Vatne, including references attached to Theorem 5.3 and Lemma D.6. This modestly improves readability and source identification. The scientific content, evidence, and limitations remain unchanged.
